pages.title: What it does
text: It drives the custom attribute rpgleveling:health_regen: how many health points you regain per second, ticked by the server.
By default it only regenerates when you are not at full health (health_regen.only_when_hurt = true) and does not require food (require_food_level = 0).
It stacks with vanilla food-based regeneration without interfering: the mod only reads the food level for the optional gate (require_food_level, default 0 = inactive) and never modifies it.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +0.125 HP/s per point.
The old curve, gain = 5 * x / (x + 40), had an initial slope of 5/40 = 0.125, so the early feel is unchanged.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: 3.333333 per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 2.0 HP/s.
The final value is the flat contribution plus the percent contribution - the design basis is additive, it does not scale the live attribute.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: Both lines are linear, so the regeneration rate keeps climbing until it meets the attribute's own range (1.0E6, unreachable in practice). There is no designed ceiling and no diminishing returns.

It still cannot make you immortal: healing is a per-second flow, so any damage source whose burst DPS exceeds it punches straight through. The ender dragon, the wither and the warden all hit far harder than the early numbers.
The mod applies no clamp by default (health_regen.hard_cap_hps defaults to 0 = disabled); the attribute's own range is the only bound. An admin who wants a backstop can set it to a positive value.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: Excellent value for a survival build: 2..3 HP/s early on already cuts down on eating and potion drinking.
If you want to shrug off chip damage, take both lines to 20..50 points.
To make the custom regeneration respect hunger too (closer to the vanilla feel), set health_regen.require_food_level to 18.
